[b]The Chamber of the Lady of the State: March 4th, 2025[/b]

Lady Theodora sat in her chambers which overlooked the sweet smelling gardens of the presidential palace, her husband had been ever stressed by the happenings which were whispered under him. She found her heart gripped with unease as he had turned to irrational and nearly unconstitutional actions which threatened his grip and seat on the government. 

Yet Lady Theodora was not a weak woman, nor servile to her husband, and she was shrewd as well in her planning. As the walls that protected the presidency were threatened, she would confer with the lady priests of Adní, the motherhood of the stars. These were the most powerful voices behind the government, being granted access to the most sacred of ears, the inner conversations of the government. Lady Theodora was one of these, but not by choice, for she had been stolen from her family and made into a sacred sister. Her marriage had caused a scandal, but she was still strong and well connected with the sisterhood. 

A knock resounded on the door of the chamber, she turned from the window, Enter! she stated, her brown eyes casting towards the door, which opened slowly to permit a woman dressed in a colorful veil.

Lady Doma, what a pleasant surprise, stated Theodora, rising to greet the chief justice of the land and the relative of her husband. 

Indeed, but I bear ill-tide my dear sister, replied Doma, embracing Theodora. 

Is that so? replied Theodora, leading Doma to a table by the window which overlooked the gardens, I grow tired of this constant bad news, it has yet been two months since my husband ascended, she stated. 

The senate made a vote today, they have voted to keep your husband in power, and avoid the recall vote, however, the Chamber of the Peoples will be investigating the vote, as it was contested due to it being a tie, replied Doma.

Theodora frowned, So they are throwing the bouncing ball around the legislature, how does this pose a threat? she enquired.

Should the vote in the Chamber of the Peoples go forward, the power that we have in the Senate might crumble. I hold that placing Τito in the place of the speaker was a bad move, he is a weaker man, he exposes our position, replied Doma. 

Then we should move to remove him? enquired Theodora.

Yes, but we must muddy the waters so that there is no suspect, replied Doma, Have him fall ill, force him to step down, she continued. 

No, not ill, he must die violently, we must drive the radical senators to a frenzy, replied Theodora.

Violence?  Why for? enquired Doma, shocked at the suggestion, I should care to remind you Theodora, that he is my brother, replied Doma, her voice rising to a slight pitch.

Someone must die my dear, we must stir the hearts of the people, then, in the hour of darkness a hero can rise, replied Theodora, her tone not changing.

What about that young Alexander fellow, he was the loudest of the senators, replied Doma.

That is quite an idea my dear Doma, I shall look into this matter, I have heard the name, perhaps I ought to pay him a visit, replied Theodora, smiling slightly. 

We can also purge his family, the Makedii, replied Doma, They are the oldest of the families that have dwelt in the republic, and their power is quite known in the northern regions, she continued. 

Hes a Makedii? enquired Theodora, her eyes lighting up as the name crossed her memory.

Yes my lady, replied Doma.

They participated in the revolution of 64, mused Theodora, His death would be most dangerous, we must be careful to keep it clean, are there any tensions in the Senate with which we might draw his death by that means? she enquired.

Perhaps, but I do not know enough of the internal workings, perhaps you should meet him as you suggested, replied Doma. 

I will, perhaps tomorrow, replied Theodora, Anything else? she enquired.

Nothing else that I can think of, replied Doma.

Then you may leave, remain steadfast my dear friend, replied Theodora as Doma rose from her seat and bowed to Theodora, before turning and leaving the chamber.

[b]The Private Dining Room of the President and First Lady:  March 4th, 2025[/b]

Consantin was not unaware to the matters which had arisen in the Senate, and while he was pleased with the outcome of the vote, he could still not yet touch the Chamber of the Peoples, who seemed to now writhe in open rebellion against the presidency.

But this was not Consantins first time in the presidency, he had served as president for 8 years almost 17 years prior, before handing the baton to his successor, as such Consantin knew how to handle the issues that beset him.

Seated at the head of the small table, the gas chandelier casting a dim shadow on the dining rooms red walls, which danced with painted frescoes of satyrs and other fanciful creatures, he enjoyed this moment of peace.

The door to the dining room opened thus permitting his wife Theodora to enter, she was a fine lady with beautiful brown eyes and a well formed face which bore traces of hidden mystery in it, she never smiled often but when she did Consantin enjoyed it.

Rising to greet her he kissed her on the cheek, a rare show of private affection that Consantin hoped showed her he still cared for her despite his recent distance to family affairs.

Servants bustled around the couple as they took their seats, napkins and cutlery laid out quickly upon the table glimmered gently under the chandelier.

The Senate was interesting today, began Consantin poking at the salad which was laid before him.

I heard, replied Theodora, The whole affair sounds dreadful, I heard that a knife was drawn, continued Theodora, her voice taking on a gentler more high pitch, servility without the truth or power thus of being servile.

And what of you my dear, how were the ladies? Enquired Consantin, referring to the ladies-in-waiting of Theodora, who at least to Consantins knowledge were the gossiping and giggling type, of which he heavily disliked.

One of them caught a cold, but the rest are as daft as always, poor girls, one wonders how they even can survive, replied Theodora in a semi-fatalistic tone.

Ah well, sounds like the usual, replied Consantin gruffly, poking at his salad.

Tell me more Consantin about the legislature today, I heard some terrible things occurred, enquired Theodora, prodding to hear his side of things.

Well the Chamber of the Peoples is planning on voting on whether to investigate the Senate vote, which I see as a waste of time, and frankly unconstitutional, replied Consantin. 

Do you intend to seek to bring this before the supreme court? enquired Theodora, If they are breaking the constitution, I would sway towards that way, she stated, taking a sip from a crystal goblet of wine. 

I might, replied Consantin, One must remain within the law, he continued.

I spoke with Doma today, replied Theodora, She said that the court would be ready to back any such moves, stated Theodora, a lie, but what would Consantin know, he never bothered to ask or verify her claims, he merely nodded appreciatively. 

I am glad for what you do, I read in the paper this morning that your polling is through the roof, you are quite popular with the citizens, stated Consantin, smiling slightly.

Am I, goodness, I hope not to overshadow you my dear, replied Theodora feigning shock.

Bah, one might consider putting you as my successor my dear, replied Consantin playfully. 

Well lets not shoot too high just yet, replied Theodora smiling as the light caught the pearls of her earrings. 

Very well, but I do believe you would make a great president, noted Consantin, raising his glass towards her. 

Well I might drink to that, replied Theodora raising her own glass slightly.

As the night waned on and the dinner continued to the final course the conversation slowly shifted to their family, Consantin VII and his brother Mikael Ptolenos III. Consantin VII had long been slated to be the successor to his fathers presidency even back towards the end of that presidency, however, his father had appointed his brother Mikael II as successor. Nevertheless it was still widely whispered among the top families of the government that Consantin VII would serve after the end of his fathers term. 

Theodora was aware of the whispers and aware of her sons prowess, he had been elected a member of the Chamber of the Peoples and held power as the head of the Presidential Party, she had quietly ensured all of this happened, and was ready to hand the baton of the presidency as soon as the end of her husband's presidency, however, her husband had his eyes on Consantins brother Mikael III, as Mikael was more militarily aligned. 

As the dinner came to an end, Theodora rose from the table, moving to kiss her husband before wishing him a goodnight, leaving him to his musing, the scent of her lavender perfume lingering in the air behind her.
